fields.description:
The IP address of the previous fingerprint. The difference between
                                 the current and previous values is one indicator that a session
                                 hijacking attack has occurred. See the CurrentIp field for the newly
                                 observed IP address.

fields.name: PreviousPlatform
fields.description:
The platform of the previous fingerprint. The difference between
                                 the current and previous values is one indicator that a session
                                 hijacking attack has occurred. See the CurrentPlatform field for the
                                 newly observed platform.

fields.name: PreviousScreen
fields.description:
The screen of the previous fingerprint. The difference between the
                                 current and previous values is one indicator that a session
                                 hijacking attack has occurred. See the CurrentScreen field for the newly
                                 observed screen.

fields.name: PreviousUserAgent
fields.description:
The user agent of the previous fingerprint. The difference between
                                 the current and previous values is one indicator that a session
                                 hijacking attack has occurred. See the CurrentUserAgent field for the
                                 newly observed user agent.

fields.name: PreviousWindow
fields.description:
The browser window of the previous fingerprint. The difference
                                 between the current and previous values is one indicator that a
                                 session hijacking attack has occurred. See the CurrentWindow field for the newly
                                 observed window.

fields.name: Score
fields.description:
Specifies how much the new fingerprint deviates from the previous
                                 one. The score is from 6.0 through 21.0. The event exposes five
                                 field pairs (such as CurrentIp and PreviousIp) to view the before and after data for
                                 browser features that contributed to this anomaly. See the
                                    SecurityEventData field
                                 for all contributing features in JSON format. A large deviation
                                 score (6.0 or more) between two intra-session fingerprints
                                 indicates that two different browsers are active in the same
                                 session. The presence of two active browsers usually means that
                                 session hijacking has occurred.

fields.name: SecurityEventData
fields.description:
The set of browser fingerprint features that triggered this event.
                                 See the Threat Detection
                                    documentation for the possible features. For example, a
                                 user’s current browser fingerprint diverges from the previously
                                 known fingerprint. If Salesforce concludes the user’s session was
                                 hijacked, it fires this event, and the contributing features are
                                 captured in this field in JSON format. Each feature describes a
                                 browser fingerprint property, such as the browser user agent,
                                 window, or platform. The data includes the current and previous
                                 values for each feature.

fields.name: Summary
fields.description:
A text summary of the threat that caused this event. The summary
                                 lists the browser fingerprint features that most contributed to the
                                 threat detection, along with their contribution to the total
                                 score.

fields.description: Identifier of the feed item, record, or file. This is a polymorphic relationship field.

fields.name: EntityKeyPrefix
fields.description:
The first three digits of the EntityID field, which identify the
           object type (account, opportunity, etc). This read-only field is available in API version
           32.0 and later. Interface label is “Record Key Prefix,” which appears only in
            reports.

fields.name: EntityType
fields.description:
The standard name for the object type (account, opportunity, etc). This read-only
           field is available in API version 33.0 and later. 

Note
Querying topic assignments for
            the ManagedContentVersion entity type isn’t supported.


Interface label is
            “Object Type,” which appears only in reports.


Tip
In most cases, you
            should use this field rather than EntityKeyPrefix, which exists
            primarily to support older reports.

fields.name: NetworkId
fields.description:
Identifier of the community to which the TopicAssignment belongs. This field is
           available only if digital experiences is enabled in your org.

fields.name: TopicId
fields.description: Identifier of the topic. This is a relationship field.

fields.name: Language
fields.description:
The combined language and locale ISO code, which
											controls the language for labels displayed in an
											application. (The values in this field are not related
											to the default locale selection.)This picklist contains the following
												fully-supported languages:

												Chinese (Simplified): zh_CN


												Chinese (Traditional): zh_TW


												Danish: da


												Dutch: nl_NL


												English: en_US


												Finnish: fi


												French: fr


												German: de


												Italian: it


												Japanese: ja


												Korean: ko


												Norwegian: no


												Portuguese (Brazil): pt_BR


												Russian: ru


												Spanish: es


												Spanish (Mexico): es_MX Spanish (Mexico) defaults to
												Spanish for customer-defined translations.

												Swedish: sv


												Thai: th
												The Salesforce user interface is fully translated
												to Thai, but Help is in English.

fields.name: NamespacePrefix
fields.description:
The namespace prefix that is associated with this
											object. Each Developer Edition org that creates a
											managed package has a unique namespace prefix. Limit: 15
											characters. You can refer to a component in a managed
											package by using the namespacePrefix__componentName
											notation. The namespace prefix can have one of the
												following values.

												In Developer Edition orgs,
												NamespacePrefix is set to the
												namespace prefix of the org for all objects that
												support it, unless an object is in an installed
												managed package. In that case, the object has the
												namespace prefix of the installed managed package.
												This field’s value is the namespace prefix of the
												Developer Edition org of the package
												developer.

												In orgs that are not Developer Edition orgs,
												NamespacePrefix is set only
												for objects that are part of an installed managed
												package. All other objects have no namespace
												prefix.

fields.name: ParentId
fields.description:
ID that identifies the topic. After a
												TopicLocalization record is created, this ID can’t
												be modified.

fields.name: Value
fields.description:
The translated text for the topic name. Label is
												Topic Name Translation.

fields.name: ActionEnum
fields.description:
The action taken by a user on a topic. The possible values are:
            LIKE

            COMMENT

            POST

            ASSIGN

            SHARE

            FAVORITE

            UNFAVORITE

            AT_MENTION

            BANG_MENTION

            COMMENT_LIKE

            USER_ENDORSEMENT

            SKILL_PEER_ENDORSEMENT

            SKILL_SELF_ENDORSEMENT

            BEST_ANSWER

fields.name: NetworkId
fields.description: ID of the Experience Cloud site where the action was performed.

fields.name: TopicId
fields.description: Identifier of the topic.

fields.name: UserId
fields.description: Unique Salesforce user ID.

fields.name: ActionConfig
fields.description:
Describes the action to take when the matching Transaction
                                 Security policy is triggered. Also indicates the type of
                                 notifications selected and the ID of the intended recipient. The
                                 recipient must be active and assigned the Modify All Data and View
                                 Setup user permissions. Multiple actions can be taken. The actions
                                 available depend on the Event Type field.

fields.name: ApexPolicyId
fields.description:
Represents the Apex TxnSecurity.PolicyCondition or TxnSecurity.EventCondition
                                 interface for this policy.

fields.name: BlockMessage
fields.description:
The custom message sent to a user when a policy blocks their
                                 action. Used in Real-Time Event Monitoring only. Maximum of 1000
                                 characters. This field is null when the default message option is
                                 selected in the UI. Available only when
                                    EventName is set to ApiEvent, ListViewEvent, BulkApiResultEventStore, or ReportEvent. Available in API
                                 version 49.0 and later.Include org- or policy-specific
                                    information in your custom message, such as the name of the
                                    responsible administrator or the business unit. Be careful about
                                    what you include. Too much information on how the policy was
                                    designed. can aid a malicious user. 
Two-factor
                                    authentication (2FA) isn’t supported in Lightning Experience, so
                                    events like ListView and
                                       ReportEvent are upgraded
                                    to Block in Lightning.
Custom messages aren’t
                                    translatable.

fields.name: CustomEmailContent
fields.description:
The administrator-created custom email content sent when a policy
                                 is triggered. Used in Real-Time Event Monitoring only. Maximum of
                                 1333 characters. This field is null when the Custom Email Content
                                 setting is selected in the UI but no message content is entered.
                                 This field is available in API version 54.0 and later.Custom
                                    messages aren’t translatable.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: The description entered for this policy.

fields.name: DeveloperName
fields.description:
The API, or program name, for this policy. Only users with View DeveloperName OR View Setup and Configuration
                                 permission can view, group, sort, and filter this field.

fields.name: EventName
fields.description:
Used in Real-Time Event Monitoring only. Indicates the name of the
                                 event the policy monitors. Valid values are:
                                    
AdminSetupEvent—Tracks metadata and configuration changes made by administrators within the Setup area of your org.

                                    
ApiEvent—Tracks
                                       these user-initiated read-only API calls: query(), queryMore(), and count(). Captures API
                                       requests through SOAP API and Bulk API for the Enterprise and
                                       Partner WSDLs. Tooling API calls and API calls originating
                                       from a Salesforce mobile app aren’t captured.

                                    
ApiAnomalyEventStore—Tracks anomalies in how
                                       users make API calls. ApiAnomalyEventStore is an object that
                                       stores the event data of ApiAnomalyEvent. This object is available in API
                                       version 50.0 and later.

                                    
BulkApiResultEventStore—Tracks when a user
                                       downloads the results of a Bulk API request. BulkApiResultEventStore is a
                                       big object that stores the event data of BulkApiResultEvent. This
                                       object is available in API version 50.0 and later.

                                    
CredentialStuffingEventStore—Tracks when
                                       a user successfully logs into Salesforce during an identified
                                       credential stuffing attack. Credential stuffing refers to
                                       large-scale automated login requests using stolen user
                                       credentials.This value is available in API 49.0 and
                                       later.

                                    
FileEventStore—Tracks when a user downloads,
                                       previews, or uploads a file. FileEventStore is a big object
                                       that stores the event data of FileEvent. This object is
                                       available in API version 57.0 and later.

                                    
GuestUserAnomalyEventStore—Tracks data
                                       access anomalies that are caused by guest user permission
                                       misconfiguration. GuestUserAnomalyEventStore is an object
                                       that stores the event data of GuestUserAnomalyEvent. This
                                       object is available in API version 60.0 and later.

                                    
ListViewEvent—Tracks when users access data
                                       with list views using Lightning Experience, Salesforce
                                       Classic, or the API. It doesn’t track list views of Setup
                                       entities.

                                    
LoginAnomalyEventStore—Stores the
                                          records of data access anomalies that are caused by
                                          potentially malicious login actions.This object is
                                       available in API version 64.0 and later.

                                    
LoginAsEvent—Tracks the login
                                          activity of admins who log in to Salesforce as other
                                          users.This object is available in API version 46.0
                                       and later.

                                    
LoginEvent—LoginEvent tracks the login
                                       activity of users who log in to Salesforce.

                                    
PermissionSetEventStore—Tracks changes to
                                       permission sets and permission set groups. 

                                    
ReportAnomalyEventStore—Tracks anomalies in
                                       how users run or export reports, including unsaved reports.
                                       This value is available in API 49.0 and later.

                                    
ReportEvent—Tracks when reports are run in
                                       your org.

                                    
SessionHijackingEventStore—Tracks when
                                       unauthorized users gain ownership of a Salesforce user’s
                                       session with a stolen session identifier. To detect such an
                                       event, Salesforce evaluates how significantly a user’s
                                       current browser fingerprint diverges from the previously
                                       known fingerprint using a probabilistically inferred
                                       significance of change. This value is available in API 49.0
                                       and later.

                                    
UniversalAnomalyEventStore—Stores data for a 
                                       broad range of system and user activity anomalies that do not map to standard 
                                       event stores.

fields.name: EventType
fields.description:
Used in Legacy Transaction Security only. Indicates the type of
                                 event the policy monitors. Valid values are:
                                    
AccessResource—Notifies you when the
                                       selected resource has been accessed.

                                    
AuditTrail—Reserved for future use.

                                    
DataExport—Notifies you when any API query
                                       is made, such as from the Data Loader API client, or when a
                                       Report export occurs.

                                    
Entity—Notifies
                                       you on use of an object type such as an authentication
                                       provider or chatter post.

                                    
Login—Notifies
                                       you when a user logs in.

fields.name: ExecutionUserId
fields.description:
Used in Legacy Transaction Security only. The ID of an active user
                                 who is assigned the Modify All Data and View Setup user
                                 permissions. As of Summer '20, Legacy Transaction Security is a
                                 retired feature in all Salesforce orgs.

fields.name: MasterLabel
fields.description:
The policy’s name.

Important
Where possible, we
                                    changed noninclusive terms to align with our company value of
                                    Equality. We maintained certain terms to avoid any effect on
                                    customer implementations.

fields.name: NamespacePrefix
fields.description:
The namespace prefix associated with this object. Each Developer
                                 Edition organization that creates a managed package has a unique
                                 namespace prefix. Limit: 15 characters. You can refer to a
                                 component in a managed package by using the namespacePrefix__componentName
                                 notation. The namespace prefix can have one of the following
                                    values:

                                    In Developer Edition organizations, the namespace prefix is
                                       set to the namespace prefix of the organization for all
                                       objects that support it. There is an exception if an object
                                       is in an installed managed package. In that case, the object
                                       has the namespace prefix of the installed managed package.
                                       This field’s value is the namespace prefix of the Developer
                                       Edition organization of the package developer.

                                    In organizations that are not Developer Edition
                                       organizations, NamespacePrefix is only
                                       set for objects that are part of an installed managed
                                       package. There is no namespace prefix for all other
                                       objects.

fields.name: ResourceName
fields.description:
Used in Legacy Transaction Security only. A resource used to
                                 narrow down the conditions under which the policy triggers. For
                                 example, with a DataExport
                                 event, you can select a resource Lead to specifically monitor
                                 export activity occurring on your Lead entities. The resources
                                 available depend on the EventType field.

fields.name: State
fields.description:
Indicates whether the policy is active. Valid values are:
                                    Disabled

                                    Enabled

fields.name: Type
fields.description:
The type of validation that the policy uses. The valid values are:
                                    
CustomApexPolicy— Created with Apex
                                       editor.

                                    
CustomConditionBuilderPolicy— Created
                                       with Condition Builder

                                 
 .

fields.name: ApexIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the Apex code used to evaluate the policy.

fields.name: BotIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the bot.

fields.name: BotSessionIdentifier
fields.description: The bot session ID.

fields.name: ClientIp
fields.description:
The IP address of the client that is using Salesforce services. A
                                 Salesforce internal IP, such as a login from AppExchange, is shown
                                 as “Salesforce.com IP”. For example: 96.43.144.26.

fields.name: CpuTime
fields.description:
The CPU time in milliseconds used to complete the request. This
                                 field indicates the amount of activity taking place in the app
                                 server layer.

fields.name: EvaluationTime
fields.description: The time in milliseconds used to evaluate the policy.

fields.name: EventName
fields.description: The name of the event, which is Transaction Security Event.

fields.name: FlowIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the flow used to evaluate the policy.

fields.name: LoginKey
fields.description:
The string that ties together all events in a given user’s login
                                 session. It starts with a login event and ends with either a logout
                                 event or the user session expiring. For example: GeJCsym5eyvtEK2I.

fields.name: PlannerIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the agent planner.

fields.name: PolicyIdentifier
fields.description:
The 15-character ID of the policy being evaluated. For example:
                                    00530000009M943.

fields.name: PolicyOutcome
fields.description:
The result of the transaction policy. Possible values are:
                                    
Error—The policy
                                       caused an undefined error when it executed.

                                    
ExemptNoAction—The user is exempt from
                                       transaction security policies, so the policy didn’t
                                       trigger.

                                    
MeteringBlock—The policy took longer than 3
                                       seconds to process, so the user was blocked from performing
                                       the operation.

                                    
MeteringNoAction—The policy took longer than
                                       3 seconds to process, but the user isn't blocked from
                                       performing the operation.

                                    
NoAction—The
                                       policy didn't trigger.

                                    
Notified—A
                                       notification was sent to the recipient.

fields.name: PolicyType
fields.description: The real time action selected for the policy.

fields.name: RequestIdentifier
fields.description: Globally unique id for a given request. For example: 3nWgxWbDKWWDIk0FKfF5DV.

fields.name: RunTime
fields.description: The amount of time that the request took in milliseconds.

fields.name: SendEmailNotification
fields.description:
Indicates whether to send an email notification. The default value
                                 is false.

fields.name: SendInAppNotification
fields.description:
Indicates whether to send an in-app notification. The default
                                 value is false.

fields.name: SessionKey
fields.description:
The user’s unique session ID. You can use this value to identify
                                 all user events within a session. When a user logs out and logs in
                                 again, a new session is started. For example: d7DEq/ANa7nNZZVD.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.description:
The access time of Salesforce services in GMT. For example,
                                    2020-01-20T19:12:26.965Z.
                                 Milliseconds are the most granular setting.

fields.name: TriggeredTimestamp
fields.description:
The time at which the Transaction Security event was generated in
                                 ISO8601-compatible format. For example:
                                 2015-07-27T11:32:59.555Z.

fields.name: Uri
fields.description:
The URI of the page that’s receiving the request. For example:
                                    /home/home.jsp.

fields.name: UserIdentifier
fields.description:
The 15-character ID of the user who is using Salesforce services
                                 through the UI or the API. For example: 00530000009M943.

fields.name: CanManage
fields.description:
Indicates whether the language is available for translation (true) or not (false).Specify translators for each language through the
                        Translation Language Setup page.

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description:
Indicates whether the translated values for this language display to users
                        (true) or not (false).

fields.name: Language
fields.description:
The language code. See the Salesforce Help for a full list of languages and
                      their codes.

fields.name: CanUseTollRoads
fields.description: Indicates if the vehicle is allowed to drive on toll roads. The default value is false.

fields.name: IsLocked
fields.description: Indicates whether the travel model record is locked or not. The default value is false.

fields.name: IsTransportingHazmat
fields.description:
Indicates if the vehicle is transporting hazardous
                                 materials. The default value is false.

fields.name: LastReferencedDate
fields.description:
The timestamp when the current user last accessed this record, a
                                 record related to this record, or a list view.

fields.name: LastViewedDate
fields.description:
The timestamp when the current user last viewed this record or
                                 list view. If this value is null, the user might have only accessed
                                 this record or list view
                                    (LastReferencedDate=)
                                 but not viewed it.

fields.name: MayEdit
fields.description:
Indicates whether the travel model record can be edited or
                                 not. The default value is false.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Name of the travel mode.

fields.name: OwnerId
fields.description: ID of the owner of this object. This field is a polymorphic relationship field.

fields.name: TransportType
fields.description:
Type of transportation. Possible values are:
                                 
                                    Bicycle

                                    
Car-Default.

                                    Heavy Truck

                                    Light Truck

                                    Walking

fields.name: SharedKey
fields.description:
This field is never read-enabled, though it is
												write-enabled. A request for this value always
												returns null.
												The value must be a base32-encoded string of a
												20-byte secret.

											You can use the Apex method Auth.SessionManagement.getQrCode() to
												get a value to write to this field.

Note
If you
												write a secret to this field, in API version 37.0
												and later the user gets an email notification that
												a new identity verification method was added to
												the user’s account.

fields.name: Type
fields.description:
The multi-factor method.
												
TOTP—The
												time-based one-time password.

fields.name: UserId
fields.description:
The ID for the user who’s associated with the
											authentication secret.

fields.name: ExternalId
fields.description:
A unique system-generated numerical identifier for the
											user.

fields.name: HasBuiltInAuthenticator
fields.description:
If true, the user has registered a
											built-in authenticator on their device, such as Touch ID
											or Windows Hello. The user can verify their identity by
											using the built-in authenticator. This field is available in API version 53.0 and
											later.

fields.name: HasSalesforceAuthenticator
fields.description:
If true, the user has connected the
											Salesforce Authenticator mobile app. The user can verify
											identity by approving a notification sent to the app. If
											the user sets a trusted location in the app, Salesforce
											Authenticator verifies automatically when the user is in
											the trusted location.

fields.name: HasSecurityKey
fields.description:
If true, the user has registered a WebAuthn-compatible security
											key. This field includes all security keys registered or
											used after Summer ’22. The user can verify their
											identity by inserting the security key into a USB port
											to generate credentials.

fields.name: HasTempCode
fields.description:
If true, the user has a temporary
											verification code generated by a Salesforce admin or
											user with Manage Multi-Factor Authentication in User
											Interface permission.

fields.name: HasTotp
fields.description:
If true, the user has connected an
											authenticator app that generates verification codes,
											also known as time-based one-time passwords (TOTP). The
											user can verify identity by entering a code generated by
											the app.

fields.name: HasU2F
fields.description:
If true, the user has registered a
											U2F security key. The user can verify identity by
											inserting the security key into a USB port to generate
											credentials.

fields.name: HasUserVerifiedEmailAddress
fields.description:
If true, the user's email address is verified.This parameter
												is available in API version 43.0 and later.

fields.name: HasUserVerifiedMobileNumber
fields.description:
If true, the user has self-registered and verified a mobile phone
											number. Salesforce can text a verification code to the
											user at that number.This parameter is available in
												API version 43.0 and later.

fields.name: HasVerifiedMobileNumber
fields.description:
If true, the user has a mobile
											phone number that was added by an administrator or
											self-registered by the user. Salesforce can text a
											verification code to the user at that number.

fields.name: UserId
fields.description:
ID of the user who’s associated with the identity
											verification methods.

fields.name: Expiration
fields.description:
The date and time when the temporary verification code expires. The code expires in 1
											to 24 hours after it’s generated. Salesforce admins and
											non-admin users with the Manage Multi-Factor
											Authentication in User Interface permission set the
											expiration time when generating the code.

fields.name: Identifier
fields.description:
The unique identifier for the temporary code. This is a
											required field that can take any value.

fields.name: TempCode
fields.description: A request for this value always returns null.

fields.name: UserId
fields.description:
The ID for the user who’s associated with the temporary
											verification code.

fields.name: AgentType
fields.description: The type of agent.

fields.name: AppName
fields.description: The app this logline has executed.

fields.name: BotIdentifier
fields.description: The unique identifier of the agent.

fields.name: BotSessionIdentifier
fields.description:
Returned with every session (from bots runtime API). The session
                                 begins with co-pilot panel is opened and ends when the user logs
                                 out of Salesforce, closes the browser tab or exits the browser. For
                                 mobile, this id is present throughout the entire time the app is
                                 open, and only changes upon cold start or logout.

fields.name: BrowserName
fields.description: The name of the browser.

fields.name: BrowserVersion

Browser major.minor version. Some browseers may not provide a
                                 minor version.

fields.name: ButtonLabel
fields.description:
When the user interacts with a message by clicking a message-level
                                 button, this is the label of the button the user selects.

fields.name: Channel

The name of the channel. For example, mobile, LEX, or
                                 Playground.

fields.name: ClientGeolocation
fields.description: Client geographic location in format Country/State.

fields.name: ClientIdentifier
fields.description: API client ID.

fields.name: ClientIp
fields.description: Client IP address.

fields.name: Components
fields.description:
An array of strings that contain the names of the components,
                                 including the namespace and the name of the component. This should
                                 include both input and output components.

fields.name: ConnectionType
fields.description: The type of connection. For example, WiFi.

fields.name: DeviceModel
fields.description: The device model.

fields.name: DevicePlatform
fields.description: The application experience

fields.name: DeviceSessionIdentifier
fields.description:
Auto-generated ID on the client-side that stays the same for the
                                 duration of the browser tab.

fields.name: FeedbackIdentifier
fields.description: The turn ID from Agents V1 API.

fields.name: HasToxicityWarning
fields.description:
Flag to identify whether the message contains a toxicity
                                 warning. The default value is false.

fields.name: IsAgentPanelExited
fields.description:
A boolean field that is true if  the user clicks on a button to
                                 navigate away from an agent panel. The default value is false.

fields.name: LightningType
fields.description: An array of strings that contains the name of the ES type(s).

fields.name: LightningTypeMessage
fields.description:
This is the ES type message associated with the co-pilot response
                                 (i.e. “Inform” or “Inquire”)

fields.name: LoginKey
fields.description:
The hash of the login id to allow tracking of all events from user
                                 login to logout.

fields.name: MessageIdentifier
fields.description: Returned with every message (from bots runtime API).

fields.name: MobileSdkAppType
fields.description: The mobile application type.

fields.name: MobileSdkVersion
fields.description: The SDK version.

fields.name: ObjectType
fields.description: The name of the object for ES Type recordInfo.

fields.name: OperatingSystemName
fields.description: The name of the operating system.

fields.name: OperatingSystemVersion
fields.description: The operating system version number.

fields.name: PageContext
fields.description: Name of the component hosting the main content of the page.

fields.name: PageObjectIdentifier
fields.description: Object id, if any, of the record being displayed.

fields.name: PageObjectType
fields.description: Object type of the page being displayed.

fields.name: PageUrl
fields.description: Raw url of the page log occurred on.

fields.name: RequestIdentifier
fields.description:
The unique ID of a single transaction. A transaction can contain
                                 one or more events. Each event in a given transaction has the same
                                 REQUEST_ID.

fields.name: SdkAppVersion
fields.description: The SDK app version this logline has executed.

fields.name: SessionKey
fields.description:
The hash of the session id to allow tracking of all events in a
                                 session.

fields.name: TaskName
fields.description: This will describe the nature of the event being logged.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.description: Timestamp at which the log event was generated.

fields.name: UiEventElapsedTime
fields.description: The elapsed time for the UI event.

fields.name: UiEventTimestamp
fields.description: Time when the message was logged according to the client.

fields.name: UiRootActivityIdentifier
fields.description:
The ID for the root activity, if any, when this message was
                                 logged.

fields.name: UserIdentifier
fields.description: The user ID of the request.

fields.name: UserType
fields.description: The type of user.

fields.name: VoiceOrText
fields.description: Whether the input by the user was “voice” or “text”.

fields.name: LeftHandSide
fields.description:
Represents the field that the filter is based on. For example,
                                    AMOUNT.

fields.name: OperatorId

Represents the filter operator. Valid values are:
                                    CONTAINS

                                    EQUAL

                                    
GE—greater than
                                       or equal

                                    
GT—greater
                                       than

                                    
LE—less than or
                                       equal

                                    
LT—less
                                       than

                                    
NE—not
                                       equal This is a relationship field.

fields.name: ParentKeyPrefix
fields.description: Represents the three-digit prefix of the parent ID.

fields.name: RightHandSide
fields.description:
Represents the value used to evaluate the component’s visibility.
                                 For example, 1000000.

fields.name: RuleId
fields.description: Represents the formula rule ID. This is a relationship field.

fields.name: AssociatedElementId
fields.description:
Represents a parent component that UiFormulaRule is associated with, such as
                      PromptVersion. This is a relationship field.

fields.name: BooleanFilter

Represents the filter logic applied to UiFormulaRule. References the UI
                      formula rule stored by UiFormulaCriterion based on the sortIndex, such as ((1
                      && 3) || 2).

fields.name: DeveloperName
fields.description:
Represents the API name of the UiFormulaRule. Note
Only users with View DeveloperName OR View Setup and Configuration permission can view, group, sort, and filter this field.

fields.name: Formula
fields.description: Represents the formula source string of UiFormulaRule.

fields.name: Language
fields.description: Represents the language of the UiFormulaRule.

fields.name: MasterLabel
fields.description: Required. Represents the label of the UiFormulaRule.

fields.name: ParentKeyPrefix
fields.description: Represents the three-digit prefix for AssociatedElementId.

fields.name: AppName
fields.description: The name of the application that the user accessed.

fields.name: BrowserName
fields.description: The name of the browser that the user accessed.

fields.name: BrowserVersion
fields.description:
The version of the browser that the user accessed in major.minor version format. Some
                                 browsers don’t provide a minor version.

fields.name: ClientGeolocation
fields.description:
The geolocation of the client in the form of
                                    <Country>/<State|Province>.

fields.name: ClientIp
fields.description:
The IP address of the client that’s using Salesforce services. A
                                 Salesforce internal IP, such as a login from AppExchange, is shown
                                 as Salesforce.com IP.

fields.name: ConnectEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser establishes a
                                    connection to a server so that it can retrieve a resource.

                                 To calculate the Transport Control Protocol (TCP) handshake
                                    time, subtract the CONNECT_START time from
                                    the CONNECT_END time.

fields.name: ConnectStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds after the browser completes the Domain
                                    Name System (DNS) lookup and begins connecting to a server so
                                    that it can retrieve a resource. 

                                 To calculate the Transport Control Protocol (TCP) handshake
                                    time, subtract the CONNECT_START time from
                                    the CONNECT_END time.

fields.name: ConnectionType
fields.description: The type of connection.

fields.name: DecodedBodySize
fields.description:
The size in octets of the HTTP message body after the removal of
                                 any applied content encoding.

fields.name: DeviceModel
fields.description: The name of the device model.

fields.name: DevicePlatform
fields.description:
The type of application experience in
                                    name:experience:form format.

fields.name: DeviceSessionIdentifier
fields.description:
The unique identifier of the user’s session based on page load
                                 time. When the user reloads a page, a new session is started.

fields.name: DomComplete
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                    readyState property is set to complete. Indicates that the
                                 page and its subresources have finished loading.

fields.name: DomContentLoadedEventEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                       DOMContentLoaded event handler
                                    completes.

                                 To calculate the processing time for the
                                       DOMContentLoaded event handler, subtract
                                    the DOM_CONTENT_LOADED_EVENT_START time
                                    from the DOM_CONTENT_LOADED_EVENT_END
                                    time.

fields.name: DomContentLoadedEventStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                       DOMContentLoaded event handler
                                    starts.

                                 To calculate the processing time for the
                                       DOMContentLoaded event handler, subtract
                                    the DOM_CONTENT_LOADED_EVENT_START time
                                    from the DOM_CONTENT_LOADED_EVENT_END
                                    time.

fields.name: DomInteractive
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                    readyState is set to interactive. Indicates that the
                                 page has finished loading, but subresources, such as images and
                                 scripts, are still loading.

fields.name: DomainLookupEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser completes a DNS lookup
                                    for a resource.

                                 To calculate the DNS lookup time, subtract the
                                       DOMAIN_LOOKUP_START time from the
                                       DOMAIN_LOOKUP_END time.

fields.name: DomainLookupStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser starts a DNS lookup
                                    for a resource.

                                 To calculate the DNS lookup time, subtract the
                                       DOMAIN_LOOKUP_START time from the
                                       DOMAIN_LOOKUP_END time.

fields.name: Duration
fields.description:
The total duration in milliseconds of the event from the
                                    START_TIME to the
                                    LOAD_EVENT_END time.

fields.name: EncodedBodySize
fields.description:
The size in octets of the HTTP message body before the removal of
                                 any applied content encoding.

fields.name: FetchStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser starts to fetch a
                                    resource from the server, not including redirects. Occurs before
                                    the DNS lookup and the connection to the server is
                                    established.

                                 To calculate the total time used to fetch a resource without
                                    redirects, subtract the FETCH_START time
                                    from the RESPONSE_END time.

fields.name: FirstInterimResponseStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser receives the first
                                    byte of the interim 1xx response from the server. 

                                 To calculate the time from when the browser sends a request to
                                    when it starts to receive an interim response, subtract the
                                       REQUEST_START time from the
                                       FIRST_INTERIM_RESPONSE_START time.

fields.name: InitiatorType
fields.description: The HTML element that initiates the resource load.

fields.name: LoadEventEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                       load event handler completes.

                                 To calculate the processing time for the
                                       load event handler, subtract the
                                       LOAD_EVENT_START time from the
                                       LOAD_EVENT_END time.

fields.name: LoadEventStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                       load event handler begins.

                                 To calculate the processing time for the
                                       load event handler, subtract the
                                       LOAD_EVENT_START time from the
                                       LOAD_EVENT_END time.

fields.name: LoginKey
fields.description:
The string that ties together all events in a user’s login
                                 session. It starts with a login event and ends with either a logout
                                 event or the user session expiring.

fields.name: MobileSdkAppType
fields.description: The mobile application type.

fields.name: MobileSdkVersion
fields.description: Mobile SDK version number.

fields.name: NavigationType
fields.description: The type of navigation timing data.

fields.name: NextHopProtocol
fields.description:
The Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) Protocol ID that
                                 fetches the resource.

fields.name: OperatingSystemName
fields.description:
The operating system name, derived from
                                    USER_AGENT.

fields.name: OperatingSystemVersion
fields.description:
The operating system version, derived from
                                    USER_AGENT.

fields.name: PageContext
fields.description:
The name of the component hosting the main content of the
                                 page.

fields.name: PageObjectIdentifier
fields.description: The unique object identifier of the event.

fields.name: PageObjectType
fields.description: The object type of the event.

fields.name: PageUrl
fields.description:
The relative URL of the top-level Lightning Experience page that
                                 the user opened. The page can contain one or more Lightning
                                 components. Multiple record IDs can be associated with
                                    PAGE_URL.

fields.name: RedirectCount
fields.description:
The total number of redirects since the last non-redirect
                                 navigation in the current browsing context.

fields.name: RedirectEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser receives the last byte
                                    of the response of the final redirect.

                                 To calculate the total redirection time, subtract the
                                       REDIRECT_START time from the
                                       REDIRECT_END time.

fields.name: RedirectStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser starts to fetch a
                                    resource that initiates a redirect.

                                 To calculate the total redirection time, subtract the
                                       REDIRECT_START time from the
                                       REDIRECT_END time.

fields.name: RenderBlockingStatus
fields.description:
The status that indicates whether the resource can block or delay
                                 the browser from rendering page content.

fields.name: RequestIdentifier
fields.description:
The unique ID of a single transaction. A transaction can contain
                                 one or more events. Each event in a given transaction has the same
                                    REQUEST_ID.

fields.name: RequestStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser starts to request the
                                    resource from the server.

                                 To calculate the total request time, subtract the
                                       REQUEST_START time from the
                                       RESPONSE_START time.

fields.name: ResponseEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser receives the
                                    resource’s last byte or when the transport connection closes,
                                    whichever comes first.

                                 To calculate the total time used to fetch a resource without
                                    redirects, subtract the FETCH_START time
                                    from the RESPONSE_END time.

fields.name: ResponseStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser receives the first
                                    byte of the response from the server. 

                                 To calculate the total request time, subtract the
                                       REQUEST_START time from the
                                       RESPONSE_START time.

fields.name: ResponseStatus
fields.description: The HTTP response status code.

fields.name: SdkAppVersion
fields.description: The mobile SDK application version.

fields.name: SecureConnectionStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser begins the handshake
                                    process that secures the connection.

fields.name: ServerRequestIdentifier
fields.description:
The request ID for the server request that’s used to find
                                 associated server logs.

fields.name: SessionKey
fields.description:
The user’s unique session ID. You can use this value to identify
                                 all events in Lightning Experience within a session. When the user
                                 logs out and logs in again, a new session starts.

fields.name: StartTime
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the browser starts to fetch the
                                 resource, including redirects.

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.description: The access time of Salesforce services in GMT.

fields.name: TransferSize
fields.description:
The size in octets of the resource, including the response header
                                 and the response payload body.

fields.name: UiEventElapsedTime
fields.description:
The difference in milliseconds between when the event is logged
                                 and when the browser tab is opened.

fields.name: UiEventTimestamp
fields.description:
The time at which this event occurs, measured in
                                 milliseconds.

fields.name: UiRootActivityIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the root activity when the event occurs.

fields.name: UiThreadResponseDelay
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds from when the browser receives the
                                 response to when it executes the callback. This delay occurs if the
                                 main Javascript thread is busy when the response is received.

fields.name: UnloadEventEnd
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                       unload event handler completes.

                                 To calculate the processing time for the
                                       unload event handler, subtract the
                                       UNLOAD_EVENT_START time from the
                                       UNLOAD_EVENT_END time.

fields.name: UnloadEventStart
fields.description:
The time in milliseconds when the page’s
                                       unload event handler starts.

                                 To calculate the processing time for the
                                       unload event handler, subtract the
                                       UNLOAD_EVENT_START time from the
                                       UNLOAD_EVENT_END time.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: The URL of the request.

fields.name: UserIdentifier
fields.description:

fields.name: UserType
fields.description:

                                 services through the UI or API.

fields.description:

                                 for specific activity subtypes. Possible values are: 
                                    Captured

                                    LegacyCall

                                    Streamed

                                    VoiceCall

fields.description:

                                    UnifiedEmail

                                    UnifiedMeeting

                                    UnifiedTask

                                    UnifiedVideoCall

                                    UnifiedVoiceCall

fields.description:
The ID of the object that contains detailed activity-specific
                                 information. The object depends on the activity type. For example,
                                 the detail for a Task activity is a Task object. The detail for an
                                 Event activity is an Event object. This field is a polymorphic relationship field.

                                 action. For example:
                                    
S—Success. Salesforce
                                       handled the request successfully. If an Apex controller
                                       throws an exception, this status is also returned. 

                                    
F—Failure. Typically
                                       4xx or 5xx HTTP codes, such as no permission to view page,
                                       page took too long to render, page is read-only.

                                    
U—Undefined

                                    
A—Authorization
                                       Error

                                    
R—Redirect. Typically a
                                       3xx HTTP code, possibly initiated by an Apex controller in a
                                       Visualforce page.

                                    
N—Not Found. 404
                                       error.

fields.description:
The category of user license. Possible values are:
                                    
CsnOnly—Users
                                       whose access to the application is limited to Chatter. This
                                       user type includes Chatter Free and Chatter moderator
                                       users.

                                    
CspLitePortal—CSP Lite Portal license. Users
                                       whose access is limited because they’re organization
                                       customers and access the application through a customer
                                       portal or an Experience Cloud site.

                                    
CustomerSuccess—Customer Success license.
                                       Users whose access is limited because they’re organization
                                       customers and access the application through a customer
                                       portal.

                                    
Guest—Users
                                       whose access is limited so that your customers can view and
                                       interact with your site without logging in.

                                    
PowerCustomerSuccess—Power Customer Success
                                       license. Users whose access is limited because they’re
                                       organization customers and access the application through a
                                       customer portal. Users with this license type can view and
                                       edit data they directly own or data owned by or shared with
                                       users below them in the customer portal role hierarchy.

                                    
PowerPartner—Power Partner license. Users
                                       whose access is limited because they’re partners and
                                       typically access the application through a partner portal or
                                       site.

                                    
SelfService—Users whose access is limited
                                       because they’re organization customers and access the
                                       application through a self-service portal.

                                    
Standard—Standard user license. This user
                                       type also includes Salesforce Platform and Salesforce
                                       Platform One user licenses, and admins for this org.
